seoTitle: How to List Multiple Sizes on eBay Using Variations (2026)
metaDescription: Learn how to add size, color, and material variations to an eBay listing from Seller Hub, manage drafts, and keep stock accurate per size.
intro: If you sell clothing, shoes, or anything with multiple options, listing every size as its own separate item wastes time and clutters your store with near-duplicate pages. eBay's variation listings let you combine sizes, colors, or materials into a single product page that buyers pick from with a dropdown, and the same listing tools are available whether you're working from the iPhone app or the desktop Seller Hub. This guide covers where the selling and sizing tools live in your account, how drafts let you build a listing over multiple sessions, and the actual steps for turning on variations so your stock stays accurate per size.

steps.heading: Find the Selling tools in your account
steps.body: Everything for managing listings sits under the Selling section of My eBay, reached from the account menu — Overview, Sell an item, Drafts, Scheduled, Active, Sold, Unsold, Payments, and Shipping labels are all grouped here. Right below Selling, the Sizes section of the account menu is where you can set your default measurement preferences, which matters once you're entering multiple size values on a variation listing so eBay displays them the way your buyers expect.

image.caption: The Selling section of the My eBay sidebar, with Overview, Sell an item, Drafts, and the other listing-management links, and Sizes just below it.

steps.heading: Enable item specifics for size, color, or material
steps.body: Before variations can be added, the listing needs item specifics turned on for whichever attributes apply — size for shoes and clothing, color for anything that comes in multiple shades, material where it's relevant. eBay uses these item specifics to build the selectable dropdowns buyers see on the listing page, so getting them named correctly up front avoids having to rebuild the variation structure later.

steps.heading: Turn on the multi-variation option in the listing flow
steps.body: When creating or editing a listing, there's a dedicated toggle for variations that switches the listing from a single fixed set of details into a template covering several sizes or colors under one product. Once it's on, eBay adds a grid where each row represents one combination — say, a shoe in size 8, 9, and 10 — instead of you creating three nearly identical listings.

steps.heading: Fill in each size and its stock separately
steps.body: Inside that variation grid, each row gets its own values: the size or color label, quantity available, and optionally its own price if certain sizes cost more due to demand or scarcity. Photos can also be assigned per variation, which matters most for color options where buyers genuinely need to see the actual shade rather than a single generic product photo covering every choice.

image.caption: The Drafts page under Selling, listing saved-but-unfinished listings you can resume — useful for building out a multi-size listing across more than one session.

steps.heading: Save as a draft if you're not finishing in one sitting
steps.body: Filling out a full variation grid with photos for every size takes longer than a single-item listing, so eBay saves incomplete listings to Drafts automatically. From there, each draft shows a Resume draft button that takes you right back into the listing where you left off, with whatever sizes and photos you'd already entered intact — useful if you're photographing each size separately and adding them as the photos come in rather than all at once.

steps.heading: List from either the iPhone app or the desktop site
steps.body: The variation workflow isn't desktop-only — the same item specifics, variation toggle, and per-size stock fields are available from eBay's iPhone app when you're listing on the go. Which one to use mostly comes down to convenience: the app is faster for snapping photos of each size right as you list, while the desktop Seller Hub gives you a wider grid view that's easier to review before publishing a listing with a lot of variations.

faq.question: Can I add size variations from the eBay iPhone app?
faq.answer: Yes, the mobile app supports adding variations like size and color directly during the listing process, not just the desktop site.

faq.question: Do I need separate photos for each size?
faq.answer: It's recommended for color variations especially, since buyers often want to see the actual option they're choosing, though it's not always required for every size.

faq.question: Can I set different stock levels for each size?
faq.answer: Yes, each row in the variation grid gets its own quantity, so you can track which sizes are selling out without affecting the rest of the listing.

faq.question: What categories support variation listings on eBay?
faq.answer: Clothing, shoes, and other items with size, color, or material options are the most common categories that support this feature.

faq.question: What happens to a variation listing I don't finish?
faq.answer: eBay saves it to Drafts under the Selling section, where a Resume draft button lets you pick back up with the sizes and details you already entered.
